grades.quote: The LR/SC sequence can be given acquire semantics by setting the aq bit on the LRinstruction.
grades.reason: Explains how aq and rl give acquire/release/sequentially consistent semantics on LR/SC atomics, including what happens with neither bit set and which combinations to avoid. It covers LR/SC rather than AMOs, so it is a useful partial answer.
A mapping table showing which C/C++ memory orders use .aq, .rl and .aqrl on AMOs and LR/SC. It shows usage but never defines what aq and rl mean.

grades.quote: via an AMO with both _aq_ and _rl_ set
grades.reason: Mentions that an AMO with both aq and rl set is fully ordered and that an LR with aq or an SC with both bits is used for TSO RMWs. This is auxiliary mapping context, not a definition of aq/rl.

grades.quote: If the _aq_ bit is set, then no later memory operations in this RISC-V hart can be observed to take place before the AMO. Conversely, if the _rl_ bit is set, then other RISC-V harts will not observe the AMO before memory accesses preceding the AMO in this RISC-V hart.
grades.reason: Directly defines aq and rl on AMOs: acquire ordering for later operations, release ordering for earlier operations, and sequential consistency when both are set. It also gives a lock acquire/release example.
